- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast early to avoid overcorrection.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast growth to 5–7% per period post-spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if recent 18-day average is below 70.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 → 0.50), model often fails to anticipate breakout — adjust forecast upward by 2–3% in first 5–7 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from history (e.g., >15% from 18-day mean), model tends to lag — apply 1–3% upward correction in next 3–5 periods.
